# Foundgine 1.1.7

Foundgine is a programmable semantic execution platform for .NET. It separates structured intent from application-owned authorization and physical provider execution.

## Canonical flow

```text
Caller → Intent → Semantic Model → Resolution → Authorization → Plan → Provider → Result + Evidence
```

## Primary website pages

- [Home](https://cristianbarragan.github.io/Foundgine/) — product problem, execution model and boundaries.
- [What is Foundgine?](https://cristianbarragan.github.io/Foundgine/what-is-foundgine.html) — semantic execution explained.
- [Getting Started](https://cristianbarragan.github.io/Foundgine/getting-started/) — canonical Supply Chain application walkthrough.
- [How it works](https://cristianbarragan.github.io/Foundgine/how-it-works/) — concrete request lifecycle.
- [Architecture](https://cristianbarragan.github.io/Foundgine/architecture/) — layers, providers and adapters.
- [AI agents](https://cristianbarragan.github.io/Foundgine/ai-agents/) — host-owned authority and safe agent integration.
- [Samples](https://cristianbarragan.github.io/Foundgine/samples/) — canonical, semantic and PenTest applications.
- [Security](https://cristianbarragan.github.io/Foundgine/security/) — host-owned identity, semantic authorization, security-preserving planning and provider conformance.
- [Packages](https://cristianbarragan.github.io/Foundgine/packages/) — all source packages and their responsibilities.
- [Agent benchmark](https://cristianbarragan.github.io/Foundgine/agent-benchmark/) — controlled agent-facing experiments.
- [Performance](https://cristianbarragan.github.io/Foundgine/performance/) — scoped performance evidence and interpretation rules.

## Boundaries

GraphQL, JSON, MCP and AI are adapters/intent sources. SQL and InMemory are providers. Authentication and identity lifecycle remain host-owned. Capability discovery is descriptive, not authorization.
